Notes: Two independent 2-bit banks. Carries MCLK out (B to A) and the two oscillator enables in (A to B). Lives on the module so the mezzanine never carries 3.3 V. Partial power-down puts both ports high impedance with either supply at ground, which protects the FPGA when a module is absent or unpowered. In the netlist only its supplies and GND are wired: all data pins, DIR and OE are open, and VCC(A) has no source. Second-source parts exist for the generic type. 0012.

The one place in the design where the specific regulator matters: this rail sets full scale, so its noise is multiplicative. Target about 10 uV across the audio band on 3.3 V. Dissipates 92 mW at 54 mA. EN/UV unconnected, so the rail is not gated at power-on. Grade and package suffix not fixed. 0009, 0012.
Oscillators, divider and translator B side, regulated separately from the element reference so the two loads do not share a rail. Dissipates 64 mW at 37.5 mA. EN/UV unconnected. 0009.

Negative post-regulator for the op amp stage. Its IN pins are unconnected in the netlist and no charge pump exists to feed them, so the rail has no source. Op amp PSRR falls steeply with frequency, so post-regulating the pump is not optional. 0009.

Part selected in 0012; the netlist symbol and footprint are an Abracon ASE stand-in with the same EN/GND/OUT/Vdd pinout but the wrong footprint. Ordering suffix for frequency, tolerance and supply not fixed. 48 kHz family, divided by two to a 24.576 MHz element clock. 15.5 mA running, 1.5 mA in standby; standby shuts the resonator down rather than gating the output.

Same part and same stand-in as Y1. 44.1 kHz family, divided by two to 22.5792 MHz. Two oscillators are required because the families sit at 147 to 160, which no divider bridges. Exactly one runs at a time. In the netlist both EN pins are driven straight from the 2.5 V header rather than through the translator.

Second half of the channel L stand-in pair. See U3a.

Channel R stand-in pair. The real part is constrained to a logic family whose input threshold is 2.0 V at a 3.3 V supply, so the 2.4 V the FPGA guarantees at 2.5 V is accepted with margin; a 0.7xVCC family would sit at 2.31 V and be marginal. That threshold is what lets 28 element lines cross untranslated. 0012.
Second half of the channel R stand-in pair. See U4a. In the netlist the Cp clock inputs of all four packages are unconnected, so no flip-flop is clocked.

Never chosen. The netlist carries an OPA1612AxD stand-in with only V+ and V- wired; both inputs and the outputs are open. Value never chosen; 1k is a placeholder and it is load-bearing, because it sets both the element reference rail current (14 x 3.3 V / R, so 46.2 mA at 1k) and the differential swing into the I/V stage (+/-23.1 mA at 1k). See power.md. Thin film is specified and must not be substituted to thick film: rotation makes 1 percent tolerance adequate but does not fix voltage coefficient within one resistor. Arrays are preferred over discretes so elements share a die. The stock Device:R_Network08 symbol is a BUSSED network (one common pin plus eight) on a 4-resistor footprint; the design needs 28 isolated elements, and as wired it shorts each package's elements together and merges SUM_P with SUM_N. 0008, 0012, model/README.md.

This is where the element switching current actually comes from: a regulator loop is orders of magnitude too slow to hold the rail at the modulator rate. 800 nF total holds a 23.1 mA redistribution step to 29 uV over 1 ns of reclock skew (power.md), so loop inductance from the package pin to the capacitor is the binding term, not capacitance. Value and package fixed; dielectric and manufacturer open.
